newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends higher on foreign fund influx.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends higher on foreign fund influx.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed higher against the U.S. dollar on Thursday, thanks largely to foreign fund inflows for the bullish stock market, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.526, back from an intra-day high of T$27.521, against Wednesday's T$27.540 close.
Turnover through dealers was a modest US$191 million.
"Foreign funds have recently accelerated their inflows because of the boosting stock market, creating upward pressure on the Taiwan dollar," said one dealer.
The stock index inched to a slightly higher close on Thursday, gaining 13.08 points to a six-year high of 8,268.15.
Another factor in the Taiwan dollar appreciation was the general softness of the greenback overseas, dealers said.
Dealers nonetheless said they saw quite active U.S. dollar buying on Thursday.
"Quarter-end U.S. dollar demand has gradually emerged, thus offsetting the local dollar's rise today," the dealer said.
Dealers said they saw near-term resistance at T$27.50.
A T$27.51-27.54 range was seen for Friday.
